examples.solution_text:
The inner function is $\dfrac{x}{6}$, with derivative $\dfrac{1}{6}$.
$\begin{align*}\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=4\times\dfrac{1}{6}\sec^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{6}\right)\\&=\dfrac{2}{3}\sec^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{6}\right)\end{align*}$

Differentiate each term, including the inner derivative for each trigonometric term.
$\begin{align*}\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=14x+4\left(5\sec^{2}5x\right)-3\left(4\cos 4x\right)\\&=14x+20\sec^{2}5x-12\cos 4x\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
Find the exact value of each derivative.
(a) $f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{16}\right)$, given $f(x)=\tan 4x$.
(b) $g'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$, given $g(x)=\sec x$.
(c) $h'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$, given $h(x)=\operatorname{cosec}x$.
By writing $\tan x=\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}$, use the quotient rule to derive $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\tan x)=\sec^{2}x$.
examples.solution_text:
Let $u=\sin x$ and $v=\cos x$. Then $u'=\cos x$ and $v'=-\sin x$.
$\begin{align*}\dfrac{d}{dx}(\tan x)&=\dfrac{u'v-uv'}{v^{2}}\\&=\dfrac{\cos x\cos x-\sin x(-\sin x)}{\cos^{2}x}\\&=\dfrac{\cos^{2}x+\sin^{2}x}{\cos^{2}x}\\&=\dfrac{1}{\cos^{2}x}\\&=\sec^{2}x\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: By writing $\sec x=(\cos x)^{-1}$, use the chain rule to derive $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sec x)=\sec x\tan x$.
examples.solution_text:
Apply the chain rule to the reciprocal power.
$\begin{align*}\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sec x)&=-(\cos x)^{-2}(-\sin x)\\&=\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos^{2}x}\\&=\dfrac{1}{\cos x}\times\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}\\&=\sec x\tan x\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: By writing $\cot x=\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}$, use the quotient rule to derive $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\cot x)=-\operatorname{cosec}^{2}x$.
examples.solution_text:
Let $u=\cos x$ and $v=\sin x$. Then $u'=-\sin x$ and $v'=\cos x$.
$\begin{align*}\dfrac{d}{dx}(\cot x)&=\dfrac{u'v-uv'}{v^{2}}\\&=\dfrac{(-\sin x)\sin x-\cos x\cos x}{\sin^{2}x}\\&=\dfrac{-\sin^{2}x-\cos^{2}x}{\sin^{2}x}\\&=-\dfrac{1}{\sin^{2}x}\\&=-\operatorname{cosec}^{2}x\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: By writing $\operatorname{cosec}x=(\sin x)^{-1}$, use the chain rule to derive $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\operatorname{cosec}x)=-\operatorname{cosec}x\cot x$.
examples.solution_text:
Apply the chain rule to the reciprocal power.
$\begin{align*}\dfrac{d}{dx}(\operatorname{cosec}x)&=-(\sin x)^{-2}\cos x\\&=-\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin^{2}x}\\&=-\dfrac{1}{\sin x}\times\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}\\&=-\operatorname{cosec}x\cot x\end{align*}$

coverage.summary: Authored eight worked examples covering every distinct retained assessment method, with one mapping for each of the 20 exact assessment locators. Practice and quiz mathematics were neither changed nor re-audited. Numerical examples use different values; the four fundamental derivative derivations retain their defining identities. New working was checked against the supplied source and mathematically verified, including correction of the cosecant factorisation printed at source line 416. Every example separates question and solution, uses single-dollar mathematics and supported continuation alignment, and leaves prose editable with automatic blue solution styling. No bare-expression continuation needs an authored phantom gutter. Diagrams and annotations are unnecessary for these symbolic methods. Actual rendering verification remains for the later capture stage.

examples.derivation: Source lines 172–174 support constant multiples of tangent. Independently applying the constant-multiple rule gives y'=8 sec²x.
Source lines 184–190 support fractional linear arguments and outer constants. With u=x/6 and u'=1/6, y'=4(1/6)sec²(x/6)=(2/3)sec²(x/6).
Source lines 99–104 and 196–210 support termwise differentiation and linear trigonometric compositions. The three derivatives are 14x, 20sec²5x and -12cos4x, giving y'=14x+20sec²5x-12cos4x.

Source lines 241–252 teach differentiation followed by exact substitution; lines 398–429 supply the reciprocal derivatives. Independently, f'(π/16)=4sec²(π/4)=8; g'(π/4)=sec(π/4)tan(π/4)=√2; h'(π/4)=-cosec(π/4)cot(π/4)=-√2. These applications match the retained assessed method.
Source lines 73–91 explicitly teach the quotient derivation. With u=sin x and v=cos x, the numerator is cos²x+sin²x=1; division by cos²x gives sec²x.
Source lines 398–407 teach the reciprocal-power chain rule. Differentiating (cos x)^(-1) gives -(cos x)^(-2)(-sin x)=sin x/cos²x=(1/cos x)(sin x/cos x)=sec x tan x.
Source lines 420–429 teach the quotient derivation. Differentiating cos x/sin x gives (-sin²x-cos²x)/sin²x=-1/sin²x=-cosec²x.

Source lines 409–418 teach the reciprocal-power chain rule. Differentiating (sin x)^(-1) gives -(sin x)^(-2)cos x=-cos x/sin²x=-(1/sin x)(cos x/sin x)=-cosec x cot x. The candidate correctly repairs the erroneous second factor printed at source line 416.
